method: Tier-0 primary source (nist.gov) fetched directly and cross-checked against independent Tier-2 corroboration (HPCwire) per policy/verification.md §1; announcement-type claims about the MOU and named initiatives are Tier-0-sufficient.
origin_items: Surfaced during cycle 1's Tier-0 sweep of nist.gov; carried untriaged into cycle 2, opened for verification this cycle.

claims.text: NIST announced on 4 August 2026 that it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Department of Energy's Office of Science to collaborate on AI-accelerated innovation under the White House-led Genesis Mission
claims.reasoning: Stated directly on NIST's own news post (Tier 0, sufficient alone) and independently corroborated by HPCwire's own reporting of the same MOU.

claims.text: NIST will execute two initiatives through its Centers for AI in Manufacturing and Critical Infrastructure (a partnership with MITRE): a manufacturing-productivity center including a drone-production project targeting a tenfold scale-up in two years, and a critical-infrastructure cyberthreat-detection center, both structured as two-year sprints
claims.reasoning: Initiative names, scope and two-year sprint structure stated directly on NIST's own post; Tier-0-sufficient for this announcement-type detail.

claims.text: NIST Director Arvind Raman said: 'Our contribution to the Genesis Mission exemplifies NIST's ongoing commitment to advancing U.S. leadership in critical technologies'
claims.reasoning: Direct quote attributed to a named official on NIST's own post.

falsifier_notes: Overall verdict: CLEAR TO PUBLISH as confirmed. dedup-check returned zero matches. Checked specifically against the already-published `meta-synaps-genesis-mission` (Meta's SAM3/DINOv3 role in DOE's Berkeley-Lab-led SYNAPS-I sub-project under the same Genesis Mission umbrella) -- treated as a separate standalone story, not a follow-up: the two describe different agencies/initiatives under the same broad program, not a continuation of the same narrower story thread, and a reader of this NIST story does not need the Meta article's specifics to understand it (only brief Genesis Mission context, given in the body). No dispute or correction found.
